 Oral Judgment

1. This appeal is by the claimants against the judgment and award 13.09.2022 passed in MVC No.1175/2019 by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-XII, Vijayapura [for short 'Tribunal'], whereby the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-XII, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. One Mahesh More met with an accident on 31.03.2019 and died.
His wife and children filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.72,00,000/- with interest.

The Tribunal considered the entire material on record and dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the claimants failed to establish that the deceased died in the road traffic accident that occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing No.MH-13/DA- 7275 on 31.03.2019.
Aggrieved by the said judgment, claimants filed this appeal on 05.12.2022 itself.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6574 HC-KAR 3.
Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.
4. The alleged accident is occurred on 31.03.2019 and the complaint was lodged after one month 25 days i.e., on 28.05.2019 and the delay in filing the complaint is not explained.
The death of the deceased Mahesh on 31.03.2019 is not in dispute.
The main contention of the learned counsel for the claimants is that there is no dispute regarding conducting of spot mahazar on 01.04.2019 and Post Mortem on 02.04.2019.
The dispute is with regard to cause of death of deceased.

In this regard,
the claimants pray for adducing additional evidence.
Claimants ought to have taken steps to adduce evidence before the Tribunal, but failed to do so.
Respondent's counsel requests that if the matter is remanded, the claimants are not entitled for any interest from the date of petition to till 05.11.2025.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6574 HC-KAR 5.

As it is the case of death, this Court finds it reasonable to afford an opportunity to both the parties adduce evidence, hence, matter is remanded to the Tribunal with liberty to both the parties to adduce evidence and to advance their respective arguments.
The Tribunal is at liberty to consider the entire evidence adduced by both the parties and dispose of the matter on merits within three months from the date of this order.
6. The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 19.11.2025 without awaiting any notice from the Tribunal.
Registry is directed to send back the records in 10 days.

sd/-
(P. SREE SUDHA) JUDGE SBS CT:RJ Sonali And Ors vs Anna And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19141694/
